title: AAPOR Code of Professional Ethics and Practices
provider: American Association for Public Opinion Research
notes: Current professional ethics code (revised June 2026) supporting voluntary participation, truthful purpose disclosure, privacy protection, appropriate method choice, accurate reporting, and limits on generalizing from samples.

title: Using in-depth interviews
notes: Read live. Supports recruiting current or likely users, using open and neutral questions, following up for detail, covering consistent topics, and focusing on stories and real examples rather than generalities. Original synthesis only.

title: Getting informed consent for user research
notes: Read live. Supports explaining who conducts the research, purpose, data, activities, uses and sharing, recording or observation, voluntariness and withdrawal, retention, and accessible evidence of consent. The lesson makes no claim that UK requirements govern other jurisdictions. Original synthesis only.

title: Analyse a research session
notes: Read live. Supports promptly extracting observations, recording what was said or done rather than interpretation, grouping observations into themes, forming findings, and identifying next actions or questions. Original synthesis only.

title: Taking notes and recording user research sessions
notes: Read live. Supports detailed records, notes based on observations rather than interpretations, recording consent, secure storage, and removing personal or confidential details when appropriate. Original synthesis only.

title: Finding participants for user research
notes: Read live. Supports tying recruitment to actual or likely users, considering different access needs, using only the participant information needed, limiting access to it, and deleting it when no longer needed. Original synthesis only.

title: Plan user research for your service
notes: Read live. Supports setting research questions and relevant user groups; describes typical small rounds for in-depth interviews and contrasts them with methods such as surveys that need hundreds of participants for clear findings. The lesson does not treat its suggested numbers as a universal rule. Original synthesis only.

title: Managing user research data and participant privacy
notes: Read live. Supports clear early disclosure, collecting the minimum needed to manage participation, secure limited sharing, deletion when no longer needed, and using data within the stated consent. Original synthesis only.

title: Entrepreneurship at a Glance 2011
provider: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
notes: Official OECD PDF read directly. Supports the EIP definitions on pages 3–4 and 15–16: entrepreneur, entrepreneurial activity, and entrepreneurship; activity inside firms without an ownership stake; entrepreneurship not limited to small firms or self-employment; not every new firm is necessarily entrepreneurial; and failure does not remove the entrepreneurial character of an attempted activity. No reuse license was verified, so this source is used for factual reference only.

title: OECD SME and Entrepreneurship Outlook 2021
provider: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
notes: Official OECD PDF read directly, especially page 114. Supports the current OECD restatement that entrepreneurship is not synonymous with SMEs or startups and concerns value-seeking activity through creation, expansion, or identifying and exploiting new products, processes, or markets. No reuse license was verified; facts only.
